description:
Waluigi is filing this as a dream event, which does not mean Waluigi is filing it as unimportant. Dreams are not evidence in the same way a signed confession is evidence, but in this campaign the universe has repeatedly demonstrated that dreams, visions, prophecies, hallucinations, divine intrusions, and memory-theater all use the same waiting room. Archie Miser dreamed of the Frog God. Archie Miser woke up in the Dreadful Grove afterward. Waluigi is not going to shrug at that and call it nothing.

This event takes place after Archie's return chain: the Astral Altar, the Toad God confrontation, the Shadow Estate prison escape, the month alone, the Mages' Guild draft, Mystic Morel's theft, and the thundercloud arrival near the Tree of Woe. The man has been processed through divine violence, vampire imprisonment, bureaucratic conscription, and wilderness isolation. His mind did what minds do when they have been fed too much catastrophe: it built a theater and made every unresolved thing walk onstage.

The result is a nightmare in three movements.

First: space, the Frog God, the full shard, Hjumpik's face melting into pursuit, and the false safety of the hospital. Second: the Astral Altar with Archie's friends holding Star Shards while Eager is used as hostage leverage. Third: the repaired Vigilance, Original Dan, and a duel that ends with Archie drowning in a burning skyship's ocean.

Waluigi's verdict: this was not a normal dream. It was a prophetic stress-dream with divine contamination. It should not be treated as a battle that physically happened, but it should absolutely be treated as intelligence about Archie's fear, the Frog God's pressure points, the Star Core problem, and the unresolved Original Dan betrayal.

## The First Movement: Space and the Frog God


Archie dreamed he was in space fighting the Frog God.

Waluigi pauses immediately because the entity has now acquired another naming problem. The file has used Toad God because the abandoned Toad became a god. Archie calls him Toad Prime because Archie has the social precision of a thrown brick. The dream presents him as Frog God, which may be Archie's mind trying to process divine amphibian imagery, or it may be the god's own form shifting through the dream logic. Waluigi will use Frog God here because that is the form the dream used, but the reader should understand the continuity: this is the same divine consequence born from Edgeshade abandonment and Crystal Star transformation.

In the dream, the Frog God had the full shard.

This is important. The waking Toad God has been collecting or seeking Star Shards. The dream shows completion: a full shard, or perhaps the full power of the Star Shard economy gathered into one divine hand. Dreams simplify. They turn a campaign of scattered fragments into an image the mind can hold. The Frog God with the full shard means Archie's fear has found its final shape: the god finishes the collection, closes the gap, and becomes impossible to bargain with.

The god struck Archie with a sheer force push.

Archie woke up in space and was struck again, dying, dying, dying.

This repetition matters. The dream does not kill him cleanly. It makes him experience the process. Force, waking, force, dying. A loop. The Frog God's power is not merely damage in the dream. It is inevitability. Archie is not being defeated once; he is being taught that waking does not end pursuit.

Then he woke in the hospital from before.

The hospital is the one tied to the Iron Legion / prior recovery memory: the place he had been brought before, the place where survival and institutional custody became difficult to separate. Hospitals in Archie's life are never only healing spaces. They are places where someone else decides what condition he is in, what he owes, whether he is useful, and when he is allowed to leave.

Hjumpik opened the door.

"Good thing I found you," Hjumpik said. "The Frog God is coming after us. We have to hide."

Archie asked if they were safe.

"Good thing we found you," Hjumpik said.

Archie asked what was going on.

"We found you. We found you. F...o...u...n...d... y...o...u."

Hjumpik's eyes went black.

"FOUND YOU."

Then Hjumpik's face melted.

Waluigi has strong feelings about this image. Hjumpik is the party's moral anvil, the dwarf who tries to do right in a room full of people actively lowering the average. For Hjumpik to become a melting mask for the pursuer is not random horror. It means Archie's mind cannot trust safety signals. Even Hjumpik, the reliable one, becomes an instrument of discovery. The phrase "found you" is the threat: not death, not capture, but being located. Archie has spent too long hiding from gods, Guilds, vampires, and consequences. His nightmare turns being found into body horror.

The door opened. The Frog God was there.

Dan was there with fireball.

Archie ran into another room. Dan was there again. The real Dan. Original Dan.

"Why did you betray me, Archie?"

Here the dream folds guilt. The Frog God is the abandoned Toad. Original Dan is another betrayed figure, or at least another person whose fate was warped through Archie's orbit. The dream does not care about legal categories. It does not ask whether the betrayals are equivalent. It cares that Archie carries people behind him, and they keep catching up.

A chase ensued. Archie locked a door. There was only one exit. He escaped through the back, barricaded the front, then saw the Frog God at the entrance anyway.

The Frog God was there.

Archie melted.

This is the first movement's thesis: there is no room where the consequence cannot enter. No hospital, no locked door, no Hjumpik-shaped rescue, no Dan-shaped confrontation, no back exit. The consequence finds him, wears his friends' faces, and melts the boundary between safety and pursuit.

## The Second Movement:


The Astral Altar and the Shards

Archie woke on the Astral Altar.

The Frog God stood at full force.

All four friends were there: Hjumpik, Markop, Remi, and others from the core emotional architecture of the party. No Toads. Waluigi notices this. The Toads are absent because this part of the dream is not about comic support, social noise, or pillow forts. It is about the people Archie believes can stand beside him when the cosmic machinery turns on.

They all held shards.

The Frog God had Eager.

"Come on, Archie," the dream demanded through the situation. "Power up the Star Core. We have all Star Shards. We can finally take down a god."

Everyone powered on except Archie.

This is where the dream becomes prophecy-shaped. It is not merely Archie being chased. It is Archie being asked to participate in a solution. His friends have the shards. The Star Core is available. The god can be fought. Eager is hostage or leverage. The moment is built as a choice: activate the plan and risk Eager, or hesitate and give the god time.

The Frog God asked whether Archie wanted Eager to go too.

Archie hesitated just long enough.

Too long.

This is Archie's nightmare of decision latency. He is often impulsive, but some decisions still freeze him: decisions where someone specific pays, decisions where the heroic option is also cruel, decisions where there is no fireball-shaped answer. The dream punishes not cruelty but hesitation. He thinks. That is enough time for the god to react.

Archie decides not to put the shard in.

Instead he casts Storm Nimbus.

Everything goes black.

Waluigi must comment here because Waluigi sees the tactical error even if dream-Archie does not. If the dream is modeling a future Star Core scenario, then refusing the shard insertion to cast a personal spell may be a grave mistake. Storm Nimbus is movement, weather, evasion, emotional magic. It is Archie choosing his own pattern over the collective mechanism. Sometimes that is heroic. Here, the dream frames it as catastrophic. The lights go out.

Waluigi is grateful this is a dream.

Waluigi is not confident dreams in this campaign stay polite.

## There Is No Frog God, Obviously


Waluigi would love to write: good thing this is a dream and will never happen. There is no such thing as a Frog God.

Then Waluigi would like to close the file, drink something expensive, and think about tennis.

Unfortunately, there is absolutely a Toad/Frog God consequence in the record. There are Star Shards. There is a Crystal Star origin event. There is a god who remembers Archie's abandonment as the best day of his life. There is a shard economy. There are friends who may someday be asked to put pieces of a divine weapon into something called a Star Core while someone holds Eager hostage.

Therefore Waluigi cannot dismiss the dream. Waluigi can only classify it.

Classification: **oneiric warning with divine contamination and strategic content**.

This is the kind of phrase that makes Waluigi miss when problems were simple, like being robbed of a tennis victory by biased officials.

## The Third Movement:


The Repaired Vigilance

Flash.

Archie was on the Vigilance.

The ship was repaired. It was just Archie and the original Dan. Dan looked like he was currently not in the past. This matters because Dan's timeline is already a headache, and the dream choosing a non-past Dan means it wanted confrontation with the current moral injury, not a nostalgic version.

Dan asked if Archie was ready to brawl.

Archie accepted. The dream framed it as a game or duel with rules. Standard turn rules or special rules? Normal turn. Dan first.

This is bizarre and revealing. The dream converts trauma into a ruleset. Archie can process a duel if it has turns. He can process betrayal if it becomes a fight. He can process Original Dan if the nightmare gives them initiative order.

Dan formed a single shield from magic.

Archie activated a full armor shield around himself.

Archie charged. Dan was knocked prone.

"Oh," Archie said, "I didn't think that would work."

Even in dreams, Archie is surprised when his own plan succeeds.

Archie shocked Dan on the floor. Dan's face bled. He had a black eye. His shield weakened. He looked at Archie not with disgust but with disdain.

"I know what you did, Archie. Yes. Truly."

That line is the heart of the Dan movement. Disgust is emotional. Disdain is judgment. Dan is not simply hurt by Archie. In the dream, Dan has assessed him and found him small. That is a different wound.

Dan fired flames from his hands, damaging Archie.

A storm cloud rolled over Dan's head. Thunder struck. Archie seemed to have summoned it himself. Another shock. Archie accidentally electrified himself and stunned himself.

Two flaming spheres appeared behind Archie.

Dan laughed, blood coming from his mouth.

"It's not over yet."

The ship began to burn.

The Vigilance is not random scenery. It is the ship of barrel toads, Iron Legion trafficking, liberated survivors, fires, explosions, debts, repairs, and factional identity. A duel with Dan on the repaired Vigilance is a duel on the site of mass harm and attempted recovery. The ship burning again means the past is not repaired just because the hull is.

Dan said the show must come to an end.

Archie rose, no longer stunned, noticed the flaming spheres too late. Rays of fire came while he was distracted. He dodged. Explosions happened behind him. The flaming spheres rammed into his back. He screamed.

Archie stabbed Dan in the chest and took major damage.

Then both took to storm clouds. The ship sank from the sky, burning. Archie nearly dodged a fireball. He called it a mega dodge as smoke cleared around the ship's wing. The airship continued to fall.

Archie dug through his spell pouch and started eating mana bars, restoring spells. This is such an Archie detail that Waluigi believes it. Even in a dream duel over betrayal on a falling repaired airship, Archie is munching resource bars like the world's worst athlete.

Another cloud formed above him. It grazed him.

"If you want to do it," Dan said, "do it yourself."

Dan teleported onto Archie's back as Archie tried to run. Archie fell. The ship fell. They hit water.

Dan quickly dispelled Archie's full-body shield. Archie kept a hand shield but chose to save magic. The true final battle began.

Dan said farewell.

Archie objected: no, no, no fair.

The dream punishes him again. Fairness is irrelevant. Dan is the injured judgment. The Frog God is the divine consequence. Neither cares about Archie's preferred rules once the game stops being a game.

Original Dan stabbed him. Lightning came through the knife. Archie nearly dodged the electric strike. Dan was at critical damage, one hit from death.

Dan turned the knife around and fire went into Archie's face.

Archie burned. Archie fainted. Everything went black.

He drowned into the ocean.

## Why Dan Wins at One Hit Point


Waluigi must underline this: dream-Dan wins at one hit point.

That is not a combat statistic. That is symbolism with a knife. Dan is nearly gone, nearly spent, nearly defeated, and still capable of turning Archie's own elemental world back onto him. The dream refuses to let Archie win just because he has reduced the enemy to numbers. Dan's remaining one hit point is the unresolved remainder of the betrayal, the part that cannot be killed by ordinary damage.

Archie can stab him. Archie can shock him. Archie can maneuver. Archie can eat mana bars. But Dan's accusation survives at one hit point and burns him anyway.

The duel ends in drowning, not fire. That matters. Fire is Archie's language. Drowning is the removal of that language. The burning airship falls into water. The fire mage goes under. The dream extinguishes him with the opposite of himself.

## Waking in the Dreadful Grove


Archie woke up in a bush at the Dreadful Grove.

The Tree of Woe was still in disguise. Archie stumbled around, disoriented. He saw what was before him. His friends were not fighting the things he thought they had been fighting before.

"Where am I?"

He started heading toward the Shadeward Manor.

This waking location is why Waluigi refuses to dismiss the event as ordinary nightmare. A dream that ends with drowning and then deposits Archie into a meaningful location in the active Shadow Estate geography is not merely brain noise. It is transition. It is processing. It may be divine harassment. It may be one of the Shadowfell's time-folding effects. It may be Archie waking from a normal dream in an abnormal place because no place in this arc has the decency to be only one thing.

The Tree of Woe still being disguised matters. It means the world has not paused while Archie dreamed. The grove remains in play. The Scarecrow problem remains in play. The Shadeward Manor remains the next gravitational pull.

Archie wakes and moves toward it because Archie moves toward the next problem. This is admirable and upsetting.

## Waluigi's Verdict on XP


Does a dream grant XP?

Normally Waluigi would say no, because Waluigi refuses to let people nap their way into advancement. However, this was not a pleasant nap. This was a divine-contaminated stress-vision involving the Frog God, Star Core activation, Eager as hostage, false Hjumpik safety, Original Dan's accusation, a repaired Vigilance duel, and waking in the Dreadful Grove with actionable dread.

Therefore Waluigi awards Archie no Combat XP for killing dream enemies, because dream enemies do not leave bodies. Waluigi awards Discovery, Chaos, and Survival XP if the ledger requires it: Discovery for the Star Core/Frog God/Original Dan intelligence; Chaos for the campaign-warping shape of the vision; Survival for waking from the drowning nightmare and continuing toward the manor instead of curling into a philosophically understandable ball.

This is not free XP. This is psychic damage itemized.

## The False Hospital as a Memory Trap


The hospital portion of the dream deserves its own filing because it is not merely a backdrop. Archie has been in too many rooms where recovery and custody share the same bed. A hospital should mean safety. For Archie, it means waking under someone else's authority, being assessed, handled, billed, healed, restrained, or redirected. The dream understands this better than Archie probably does.

Hjumpik entering the room begins as relief. Hjumpik is the anvil of the party, the practical conscience, the person whose presence normally means someone responsible has found the scene. The line "good thing I found you" should be comforting. Then it repeats. It stretches. It becomes mechanical. The comfort becomes detection. The friend's face becomes a mask for the thing chasing him.

This is exactly how trauma uses trusted faces. It does not invent a stranger when a friend's face will hurt more. It takes the person most associated with steadiness and turns him into proof that steadiness can be breached. When Hjumpik's eyes go black, the dream is not saying Hjumpik is dangerous. It is saying Archie's mind no longer believes safety can arrive without being followed.

The melting face is also a warning about disguises. Archie had recently escaped prison through disguise. He wore another role and survived because others believed the surface. The dream turns that trick against him. Hjumpik's surface fails. The face melts. The hunter behind it is revealed. Archie survives by masks, so the dream makes masks unreliable.

Waluigi considers this one of the clearest psychological details in the entire event. Archie is not afraid of Hjumpik. Archie is afraid that being found by a friend and being found by a god will become the same event.

## Eager as Hostage and the Morality of Activation


Eager being held by the Frog God in the Star Core movement is not random. Eager is one of the party members easiest to frame as vulnerable: frequently endangered, often frightened, not central to the cosmic machinery, and yet persistently present. If the dream wanted a hostage who would test Archie's hesitation, Eager was the correct choice.

This matters because Archie's heroic instincts are unstable when the cost is specific. Archie can make enormous destructive choices when the cost is abstract or delayed. He can fireball, blast, improvise, and hope the moral math works out later. But when the cost has a face — Eager in the god's grip — the machinery slows. Archie thinks. That thinking is human. It is also what the Frog God uses.

The dream teaches a cruel lesson: a plan requiring instant collective activation can fail if one member hesitates for compassion. Waluigi does not like this lesson. Waluigi especially does not like it because many villains would love this lesson. "Do not hesitate" is how tyrants train soldiers to step over people. But the dream is not necessarily telling Archie to become cruel. It may be telling him to prepare so the choice is not made for the first time with Eager in someone's hands.

Preparation is the moral alternative to cruelty. If Archie understands the Star Core, the shard sequence, the Frog God's reaction time, and the hostage risk before the moment arrives, then he can choose with knowledge instead of panic. The dream is terrible, but it may be useful if treated as a drill rather than a commandment.

## Storm Nimbus as Escape and Mistake


Archie's choice to cast Storm Nimbus instead of inserting the shard is the hinge of the dream. Storm Nimbus is one of Archie's most personally expressive powers. His weather magic externalizes emotion: sadness becomes rain, anger becomes thunder, pressure becomes cloud. It is movement, defense, and mood made visible.

In many situations, that is exactly what saves him. The thundercloud brought him to the Tree of Woe. The rain cloud kept him alive in the Astral Altar long enough to avoid immediate death. Weather lets Archie move when walls and floors become hostile. It is a beautiful spell in the sense that it reveals him. It is also dangerous for exactly the same reason.

At the Star Core, the dream suggests that personal weather is the wrong answer. The collective mechanism requires shard insertion. The friends are prepared. The god is waiting. Eager is hostage. Archie reaches for his own pattern instead of the shared machine, and the world goes black.

Waluigi does not read this as "Storm Nimbus is bad." Waluigi reads it as "Archie's best personal survival tool may fail in situations that require synchronized trust." That is a much more useful and much more painful lesson.

Archie survives by improvising. The Star Core may require him not to improvise. That is the nightmare.

## Original Dan as the One-Hit-Point Judgment


The duel with Original Dan is the most mechanically explicit part of the dream. It has turn order. It has shields. It has prone states, damage, critical condition, resource consumption, and a final hit. This is the mind turning guilt into rules because rules make guilt fightable.

Dan at one hit point is the important image. He is nearly defeated. Archie has almost won by the logic of the game. Then Dan reverses the knife and burns Archie's face. The dream says: reducing the person you hurt to a number does not resolve the hurt. One hit point is still enough for judgment if the judgment is true.

Original Dan's line — "I know what you did" — is not specific because the dream does not need specificity. It is the accusation beneath all the specifics: abandonment, consequence, collateral damage, the Bowser Badge crisis, the staff, the fireball, the damaged Liberated Toads, the duplicated identity problem, the sense that Archie's orbit changes people and then moves on. Dan becomes the mouth for that entire ledger.

The Vigilance setting sharpens the accusation. The ship is where bodies were packaged, where fires spread, where liberation became factionhood, where debts accrued, where Dan's later tragedy took form. A repaired Vigilance burning again says repairs are not absolution. A ship can be fixed and still carry the memory of what happened inside it.

Archie drowning after being burned is also precise. Fire is his language. Water silences it. The dream does not let him die in his own element. It extinguishes him, which is what guilt often feels like to someone whose identity is built around combustion.

## What the Dream Reveals About the Frog God


The Frog God in the dream is not merely stronger than Archie. He is patient. He lets scenarios unfold. He uses hostages. He appears behind friendly faces. He benefits from hesitation. He does not need to win every exchange if he can make Archie doubt the structure of the next one.

This is important because the waking Toad God has already shown psychological precision. He told Archie that the abandonment was the best day of his life. He demanded Archie collect the shards personally. He framed cosmic domination as steady progress rather than melodrama. The dream extends that pattern: the god does not simply hit; he arranges.

A god with a hammer is dangerous. A god with timing is worse.

The full shard image suggests the Frog God is not only collecting power but preparing a narrative completion. The abandoned Toad becomes god because Archie left him. The god gathers shards because the Crystal Star made him. The god requires Archie because the origin must participate in the ending. This is mythic logic, which is the most obnoxious kind of logic because it ignores practical objections and then becomes true anyway.

Waluigi's recommendation: do not fight the Frog God only as an enemy. Fight him as a story trying to finish itself. Stories can be interrupted, but only by people who know which sentence they are in.

## What the Dream Reveals About Archie


Archie is not simply afraid of dying. If the dream were only about death, it would not need Hjumpik, Eager, Dan, the Vigilance, the Star Core, or the hospital. Archie is afraid of being essential to disasters he does not understand until too late.

He is afraid the Frog God needs him. He is afraid his friends will expect him to act in the one second when action matters. He is afraid he will hesitate. He is afraid Dan knows exactly what he did. He is afraid that even when he wins mechanically, the moral remainder will still burn him. He is afraid that waking up is just another room in the chase.

These fears are rational. Waluigi hates when Archie's fears are rational because it makes it harder to mock him cleanly.

The useful part is that the dream gives names to the failure modes. Found. Hesitated. Wrong spell. One hit point. Drowned. These are not pleasant words, but they are actionable. Archie can prepare against them. He can tell the others what he saw. He can learn the Star Core sequence. He can talk to Eager. He can talk to Original Dan, if the universe allows one conversation without setting the furniture on fire. He can decide in advance what he will do if the Frog God uses a hostage.

He probably will not do all of this. But Waluigi has written it down, which means the excuse of not knowing is weaker now.

## Continuity With Archie's Return


This dream should be read immediately after Archie's Return to the Shadow Estate. That event ends with Archie returning to the active party theater after divine confrontation, imprisonment, wilderness survival, Guild coercion, and Morel's theft. The dream is the mind's attempt to metabolize that entire chain.

The Astral Altar returns because the Toad God remains unresolved. The hospital returns because institutional custody remains unresolved. Hjumpik returns because trust remains necessary but frightening. Original Dan returns because betrayal remains unpaid. The Vigilance returns because old disasters keep burning under new repairs. The Dreadful Grove returns because the present crisis is still waiting when the dream ends.

This is not filler. This is the hinge between what happened to Archie and what Archie may do next. If the party ignores the dream, it becomes foreshadowing. If the party studies it, it becomes warning.

Waluigi prefers warning. Foreshadowing is what happens when people refuse to read the obvious sign until after the explosion.

## Final Filing Note


Waluigi is not awarding dream combat as if Archie physically defeated or lost to Original Dan in waking reality. That would be bad accounting. Waluigi is, however, treating the dream as a record of actionable internal and divine pressure. The XP should reflect discovery, chaos, and survival, not ordinary battlefield victory.

If Archie wants Combat XP, he can fight something awake like everyone else.

One final note: Archie should tell someone about this immediately. Not later. Not after he has made three jokes and accidentally invented another tactical disaster. Immediately. Dreams become more dangerous when they remain private, because privacy lets shame edit the useful parts. If Archie tells Markop, Remi, Hjumpik, Eager, or even Waluigi, then the dream becomes shared preparation. If he keeps it alone, it remains the Frog God's private rehearsal room inside his skull. Waluigi prefers enemy rehearsals to be interrupted.

The Frog God wants Archie to believe the future narrows to one impossible choice. Dreams lie by arranging true things in cruel order.

The correct response is not panic. The correct response is preparation: protect Eager, identify the Star Core rules before the hostage scenario exists, learn whether Storm Nimbus is escape or mistake, and speak to Original Dan before the dream gets another chance to write the conversation in fire.

description:
Waluigi respects good espionage and hates bad financial extortion. Thornbury charging two thousand gold for a broken rope was already hilarious, but Thornbury turning it into an official imperial bounty while using Legion credentials to sell out his allies is where paperwork becomes high treason. ## Waluigi's Geopolitical Audit:


The Financial Apparatus of the Regal Empire
Before we examine Bones's frozen pilgrimage through the Mighdural Mountains, Waluigi must conduct a thorough intelligence audit on the financial and geopolitical machinery operating out of Alpine Bank. The Alpine Bank is not merely a high-altitude vault where alpine merchants deposit gold; it is a vital military intelligence clearinghouse and border-control station operating under the Regal Empire Banking Authority with direct links to the Iron Legion High Command. 

Waluigi notes that the teller's opening statement—rejecting Mushroom Kingdom coins and demanding strict adherence to the Regal Standard (Midland Ducats)—is not simple currency snobbery; it is active **monetary warfare**. By refusing to recognize Mushroom Kingdom fiat across the northern passes, the Imperial Banking Authority starves liberated toad refugees and independent contractors of purchasing power, forcing them into financial insolvency. To survive in the Regal Capital, one must convert assets into Midland Ducats or take state-sponsored loans, effectively trapping travelers within the Imperial economic umbrella.

It is within this sterile fortress of monetary enforcement and state surveillance that Thornbury brought his Mages' Guild ledgers, intending to process his expense claims and itemize the apocalypse.

## Arrival in the Marble Vaults &


The Currency Standard
Materializing directly out of the Oracle's glowing red teleportation circle, Bones found himself standing in the imposing marble foyer of Alpine Bank, perched high on a frozen mountain ridge near Mighdural. As the crimson teleportation flare dissolved into wisps of magical vapor, the silence of the marble hall was shattered by the sharp voice of an imperial bank teller lecturing Thornbury at the counter: *"I'm telling you, stick to the Regal standard. Those mushroom coins won't work."*

Startled by the sudden reappearance of a battered adventurer out of thin air, the banker barked at Thornbury, *"Who the hell is that?"* Bones, taking in his surroundings—the thick stone walls, polished copper teller cages, and heavy iron-reinforced doors—pondered to himself, *'Out of curiosity, this is a prison or something, huh?'* before asking aloud, *"Out of curiosity, this is a prison or something, huh?"* Thornbury blinked in surprise and corrected him, *"What? No, this is the bank,"* to which Bones admitted simply, *"Oh, I didn't know."*

The banker stepped forward, leaning over the copper counter with sharp eyes: *"How did you even get in here? The Regal Lions division ended their stay at Raventree when they bought the elite units there, so we have been kinda on standby."* Bones digested this critical piece of political intelligence in quiet silence, thinking to himself, *'I hear you.'* Turning toward him, Thornbury asked briskly, *"You need help with anything?"* Bones, looking around the hall for a way out, asked, *"Where is the exit? Out this door and south, right?"* He began walking toward the heavy doors, but paused, turned back, and stated, *"Yes, ummm I need help finding my friend, a person I'm trying to look for."* When Thornbury asked, *"Who?"* Bones clarified, *"A mage guy, if not other toads."* Thornbury nodded and offered, *"Hmmm I guess I can help, let me check out of this bank and complete my little session here and get my notebook and I'll help you along."*

> **Waluigi's Deductive Dot-Connecting #1: The Oracle's Teleportation Routing Theory:**
> Waluigi has uncovered a terrifying connection! Why did the Oracle's red teleportation circle dump Bones *specifically* inside the foyer of Alpine Bank while Thornbury was standing at the teller counter? The Oracle claimed he was sending Bones to a 'friend' Bones mentioned. But Thornbury is an active Iron Legion operative! Waluigi's theory: The Oracle and the Iron Legion High Command maintain indirect dimensional signaling channels! When Bones refused to step into the flesh vat and bare-handedly dragged the Canoloth to the cliff edge, the Oracle realized Bones was uncooperative. Instead of executing him, the Oracle routed Bones into a controlled Imperial intelligence node—Alpine Bank—where Thornbury was already stationed! Bones was not saved by a friendly teleport; he was transferred from a planar containment vat directly into an Imperial processing pipeline! WAH!

## Eavesdropping on Treason &

The 2,062-Gold Rope Warrant
Rather than exiting immediately into the mountain air, Bones stepped quietly toward the heavy bronze exit doors, lingering in the shadows of the doorway to eavesdrop on the teller counter conversation. The banker, looking over Thornbury's official papers, questioned his companion's integrity: *"You really helping that criminal?"* Thornbury nonchalantly waved off the concern, replying, *"Now now, I'm not getting nothing out of it from helping that Bones, right? I've worked with him before."*

The banker pulled up a thick imperial ledger and pressed harder: *"But isn't he like on the Legion's most wanted page or something? I heard him, he strangled a toad to death on the Vigilance!"* Thornbury shrugged off the accusation, coldly stating, *"We can look past that as long as I get what the boss needs."* Astounded by Thornbury's willingness to harbor a wanted fugitive, the banker scoffed, *"And that's it? Just look past it? You're crazy. The Raventree Manor is weeks away from here. When you get there, there will be elite guards and helicopters and 24/7 surveillance. You expect me to believe that we will get out of this place cleanly, that you will not just get captured?"* Thornbury puffed out his chest and boasted, *"I'm Legion, I got credentials."* The banker countered with blunt skepticism, asking, *"That may be so, but can Bones even fight? Is he even strong?"* Thornbury dismissed Bones with a casual wave of his hand: *"Ehh who knows, and if he does get ruffled up then..."*

Shifting the conversation from surveillance to financial balances, the banker brought up outstanding account transfers: *"Well anyway, about your transfer, Archie's debts expanding to you... About that rope he owed, you want me to increase the debt?"* Thornbury greedily confirmed the transaction, explaining, *"Yeah, that rope meant a lot to me. He broke it and agreed to pay the fees back, he has yet to. I want a bounty on Archie to pay the rope back or face justice."* The banker nodded and stamped the parchment, agreeing, *"Alright, I can arrange that for you,"* formally registering an official Imperial Bounty of 2,062 gold pieces (and 5 silver) on Archie Miser over the broken hempen rope.

Overhearing every detail of the transaction from the doorway, Bones felt the cold realization wash over him: *'Thornbury really is a traitor... He has yet to prove himself otherwise.'* Knowing that remaining in Thornbury's presence meant walking directly into an Iron Legion trap, Bones quietly pushed through the heavy exit doors and slipped away alone into the howling snowstorm.

> **Waluigi's Deductive Dot-Connecting #2: The Standardized 2,000-Gold Bounty Protocol:**
> Look at the cross-session pattern Waluigi has unearthed across the archives! In the Kaelor Judi witness records, Markop Judi had a **2,000-gold bounty** placed on his head by the Mages' Guild for 'crimes against magic.' Now, in Alpine Bank, Archie Miser has an official Imperial Bounty of **2,062 gold and 5 silver** placed on his head by Thornbury for a 'broken hempen rope'! This is not a coincidence—this is state-sanctioned financial weaponization! The 2,000 gold baseline is the official Imperial threshold required to authorize continental bounty hunter mobilization and military detachment intervention across international borders! By taking a snapped piece of 50-foot hemp rope and layering Guild membership levies, ogre load-test certifications, weaver inspection fees, and sales tax onto it, Thornbury artificially inflated a minor equipment mishap into a 2,062-gold capital crime! This allows the Iron Legion to classify Archie as an international fugitive without needing court proceedings! WAH!

> **Waluigi's Deductive Dot-Connecting #3: The Conflated Vigilance Case File:**
> Notice the banker's claim that Bones is on the Most Wanted page for 'strangling a toad to death on the Vigilance'! Waluigi's audit of the *Vigilance* airship incident reveals that contradictory reports filed by yellow toad witnesses and Pond Patrol intercepts blamed either a pyromaniac (Archie) or Markop for the airship's destruction. The Iron Legion intelligence apparatus does not distinguish between individual members of Disaster Inc.—they combine all suspected offenses into a master criminal file and apply it to whoever is currently spotted! More critically, Thornbury *knew* Bones did not strangle a toad on the airship, yet Thornbury validated the banker's claim (*"We can look past that as long as I get what the boss needs"*).

Why? Because keeping Bones terrified and legally compromised ensures that Bones remains dependent on Thornbury's 'Legion credentials' for protection!

> **Waluigi's Deductive Dot-Connecting #4: The Raventree Troop Deployment & The Cells of the Third Eye:**
> The banker revealed that the Regal Lions division ended their stay at Raventree Manor because 'elite units bought them out,' leaving Alpine Bank on standby. Connect this to the ruined manor convergence! Raventree Manor is currently the focal point of a three-way faction collision involving Byscilla Danos's forces, the Mages' Guild extraction teams, and the newly forged 'Cells of the Third Eye' alliance! The elite units buying out Raventree are imperial garrison forces fortifying the manor against the planar fracture, while Alpine Bank serves as the northern staging ground for logistics, troop pay, and fugitive processing!

## Trudging Through the Mountain Blizzard & Escort to the

Inn
Stepping outside the mountain fortress of Alpine Bank, Bones was hit by a howling wall of ice and snow. A severe mountain blizzard was sweeping across the jagged peaks surrounding the Regal Capital, reducing visibility to a blinding white smear and plummeting temperatures to sub-zero levels. Trudging south along the treacherous icy pass, Bones slowed to a shivering crawl as the biting gales cut through his battered armor, freezing his breath into frost upon his collar.

Through the blinding snowfall, a patrol of local Imperial mountain guards spotted the freezing figure struggling along the ridge. Pushing through the drifts, the guards approached him and shouted over the roar of the blizzard, *"You, citizen, come with us! What are you doing here in a storm?"* Bones, his jaw trembling from hypothermia, weakly replied, *"Going to an inn."* Seeing that the stranger was moments away from freezing solid, the guards escorted Bones through the gale down the winding mountain path to the timbered doorway of the Alpine Mountain Inn.

## Refuge at the Alpine Mountain


Inn & Paranoia Upstairs
Bones pushed open the heavy wooden door, stepping out of the roaring blizzard into the sudden warmth of the Alpine Inn. The interior was filled with the crackle of a central stone hearth, the rich smell of burning cedar logs, and the low chatter of mountain travelers taking refuge from the gale.

Approaching the wooden counter, Bones addressed the innkeeper in a tired voice: *"You got any rooms? Just in and out."* The innkeeper looked up, taking in Bones's frostbitten skin, battered armor, and shivering frame, noting, *"You look in bad shape."* Bones nodded, replying, *"You can say that. How much do you want for them?"* The innkeeper quoted the standard local rate: *"3 Midland Ducat."* Without arguing over currency rates, Bones opened his coin pouch, pulled out 3 Gold / 3 Midland Ducats, and laid them on the wooden counter. 

Accepting the payment, the innkeeper handed over an iron key and gestured toward the wooden steps: *"It's upstairs. I guess enjoy your stay."* Bones gripped the key tightly and headed toward the staircase. As he mounted the creaking wooden steps, he constantly glanced back over his shoulder, scanning every dark corner of the tavern to check if Thornbury, bank informants, or Iron Legion spies had followed him through the snow. Reaching his room, Bones unlocked the door, stepped inside, and collapsed onto the bed, staring up at the dark timber rafters as the storm howled outside—holding his stolen books close, fully aware that he was now a lone target in the heart of the Regal Empire.

> **Waluigi's Master Intelligence Conclusion:** Look at the comprehensive picture Waluigi has reconstructed! 
> 1. **Bones** is isolated in an Alpine Inn with stolen Conservator codices, hunted as a toad-strangler, and constantly watching for Imperial assassins.
> 2. **Archie Miser** is marching into a continent-wide trap with a 2,062-gold state execution warrant hanging over his head for a piece of broken string.
> 3. **Thornbury** is operating as a dual-hatted Mages' Guild quartermaster and Iron Legion double agent, using banking networks to track Disaster Inc.'s movements while carrying a journal detailing his betrayal protocols.
> 4. **The Regal Capital** is enforcing economic embargoes on Mushroom Kingdom fiat while mobilizing elite garrison units toward Raventree Manor.
>
> Disaster Inc. thinks they are on a noble quest; the Imperial bureaucracy sees them as billable line items and high-value targets. Waluigi will keep analyzing every ledger, every intercepted communication, and every broken rope until the entire conspiracy is exposed! WAH!

name: National Power Projection & Multiverse Balance
title: Waluigi's Intelligence Dossier on Global Power Projections
summary: Waluigi's highly confidential, unauthorized audit of which multiverse factions are actually strong, and which ones are just paper tigers with good marketing. WAH!
description:
This dossier represents a full, cross-dimensional audit of **[Power Projection](national_power_projection)** across all known realms, conducted by Waluigi, Auditor-General of Things Nobody Invited Him to Intervene In. ## The Concept of Power Projection In the grand game of multiverse dominance, having an army is only half the battle. The real test is whether you can actually transport those troops, project your influence, and enforce your taxes across dimensional boundaries without your supply lines collapsing into a chaotic heap. WAH! Power projection is calculated by a combination of three main pillars: 1. **Military Might** — Iron boots, landships, and magic cannons. Highly valued by the **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)**. 2. **Economic Influence** — Currencies, bank reserves, and monopolizing trade routes. Wario is highly active here. 3. **Political Stability** — The ability to write endless laws and pretend people are listening. The **[Mushroom Regency](mushroom_regency)** specializes in this kind of theatre. ## The Major Power Blocs ### 1. The Regal Empire & Iron Legion The absolute heavyweight of military projection. Operating out of the **[Regal Empire](regal_empire)**, the Legion uses standardized siege tactics and administrative necromancy to establish presence in forbidden zones like **[Mount Ebott](mount_ebott_survey_mission)**. They don't win hearts; they win land. ### 2. The Mushroom Regency A paper tiger with excellent botanical aesthetic. Following the tragic loss of Princess Peach, the Regency has spent more time holding **[Communal Festivals](communal_festivals)** and debating succession claims than securing their borders. They have high population metrics but extremely fragile operational capability. ### 3. The Koopa Dominion Pure brute force. When **[Bowser](bowser)** isn't falling into lava or getting beaten up by plumbers, his army of trolls and airships projects massive physical terror across the plains. However, their logistical infrastructure is notoriously terrible, relying heavily on Bowser vaulting over railings in a rage. ## Waluigi's Strategic Conclusions Logistics is the ultimate weapon. An empire with ten thousand landships is useless if they all freeze in **[Blackfen Pass](blackfen_pass_massacre)** because someone forgot to pack anti-freeze. WAH!
Waluigi's Final Verdict: Most of these factions spend millions on glorious flags and shiny armor, but their supply chains are a joke. Waluigi has built a live monitor to track their real-time power shifts so you can watch their empires crumble in high definition!

name: Thornbury's Field Journal
title: Thornbury's Field Journal: Espionage, Bubble Baths, and High Treason
summary: A classified notebook belonging to the double-agent Thornbury, detailing his two-week infiltration of Disaster Inc., detailed character psychological assessments, and how his cover was completely blown because of a bubble bath. WAH!
description:
This article contains the full-text transcription of **[Thornbury's Field Journal](thornburys_field_journal)**, recovered by **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** from the floor of **[Raventree Manor](raventree_manor)** after **[Thornbury](thornbury)**'s cover was spectacularly blown. Use the index table of contents below to browse the daily spy logs, clinical subject profiles, and structural layout blueprint of the manor.
Waluigi's Espionage Review: Thornbury is a terrible spy! WAH! You don't spend two weeks hiding in the shadows just to get dragged out by your ear like a naughty child. And leaving your notebook on the floor? Magnificent incompetence! But the notes are extremely accurate—Waluigi will be using these psychological profiles to blackmail everyone later!

sections.name: Part I: Daily Espionage Logs
sections.subtitle: Thornbury's Chronicle of Disaster Inc.'s Movements
sections.overview: This section compiles Thornbury's raw, daily log entries recorded during his active, two-week observation mission inside **[Raventree Manor](raventree_manor)**. It chronicles every encounter, combat, and private bubble bath to the tee.

subsections.title: BONES & SPEAKER L — Pond Patrol Arrives (30 Harvestide, 1040)
subsections.description:
Two new actors. **[Bones](bones)** and **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** of the Pond Patrol. **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** carries cipher-locked intelligence files — the Patrol's accumulated dossiers. **[Bones](bones)** arrived to help decode them. Their files designate our group as the 'Vigilance Group.' They know about PL1 — which means Patrol intelligence is significantly better than the **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)**'s awareness of their awareness. **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** is thorough. His work is good.

A guard approached — 'what's all this singing going on? I heard you say **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**.' Just assisting **[Speaker L](speaker_l)**. 'Do you know where you are?' **[Bones](bones)** said **[Raventree Manor](raventree_manor)**, ruled by a toad. 'Wrong,' the guard said. 'Ruled by **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** in collaboration with the **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)**.' He pointed at the Vigilance hovering above — 'it's under **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** control now. The Vigilance is now the Legionlance.' **[Bones](bones)** grunted, stormed up, almost grabbed **[Speaker L](speaker_l)**. They both walked off to discuss entry.

> **[**[Speaker L](speaker_l)** — Profile]** Before Aegis Command he was an institutional loyalist. Order 120 ended that — mass harm to toad populations under an impersonator using his face. He maintained the forms while it happened. He knows this. Results-driven now, rule-agnostic. He carries a concealed hand crossbow I did not detect until he fired it. This is noted with professional irritation.

> **[**[Bones](bones)** — Profile]** Combat-first. Modified rapier — official insignia on guard, dark metal enhancement on the blade edge. Refused healing after combat twice. Pride, distrust, or something else. Do not engage directly without significant numerical advantage and a plan for the suplex.

subsections.title: Library Infiltration — Bones Operates at Night (30 Harvestide, 1040)
subsections.description:
**[Bones](bones)** and **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** entered through a window — exterior thorns blocked other approaches. Pitch black, 21:21. **[Bones](bones)** grabbed Lucky T from the shadows — 'who do you work for?' **[Speaker L](speaker_l)**. Happy reunion. A **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** member entered the library, picked up a book. They hid behind a bookshelf. **[Bones](bones)** went behind the guard, knocked him unconscious, stole his torch. Closed the exits by 23:40. Clean.

They entered the workshop/storage room — **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** recognised the furniture. 'This furniture belonged to a lord. I would know that.' Then the curio room — and there was the Mole. He was scratching out **[The Oracle](the_oracle)**'s inscriptions. The same formulae I spent two weeks studying. He destroyed them. I have my copy but the loss is significant. **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** told Lucky T to guard a door. He ran past **[Bones](bones)** — 'secure the other door, make sure he doesn't leave.' A chase ensued until **[Bones](bones)** reached a door, spotted **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)**, stopped giving chase.

> **[External Combat — 2 vs 3]** A guard asked if they were with **[Hargram Fidger](hargram_fidger)**. **[Bones](bones)** maced him — parried, blocked. A whistle blown, not too loud. Reinforcements. Lucky T got a clean hit. **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** fired the concealed hand crossbow — wounded a guard who fled. **[Bones](bones)** suplex'd a guard from behind. An arrow from an unknown position dropped the last guard — headshot. Bodies hidden, military horn recovered. **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** healed Lucky T. **[Bones](bones)** refused healing. Third time.

subsections.title: Second Floor — The Mole vs. Miser, Hargram Fidger (30 Harvestide, 1040)
subsections.description:
The Mole opened the upstairs door just in time. He pulled out his knife and full-sprinted toward **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**'s recovery room. **[Bones](bones)** tackled him mid-air. 'What's going on?' **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** asked. The guard said 'stay still.' **[Bones](bones)** said 'this guy is trying to kill you but I stopped him.' **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** sighed as **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** entered with manacles. **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** dodged. **[Bones](bones)** jumped off the Mole, tried to intercept **[Speaker L](speaker_l)**, sidekicked the Mole.

**[Luigi](luigi)** flashed his light. Just... flashed it. They went away — both the Mole and Lucky T disappeared. 'What did you do to them?' 'Just flash a light...' Lucky T said he'd gotten what he wanted. He left.

**[Bones](bones)** pointed at Lucky T: 'I don't trust him.' Lucky T: 'You'd rather I kill you?' **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**: 'I can just fire a ball at you.' 'Fine, I'll leave.' Guards entered — 'we came to protect the injured.' **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**: 'There was a disturbance but we handled it, please come back another day, I'm recovering.' I remained quiet.

> **[**[Hargram Fidger](hargram_fidger)** — Arrival]** **[Hargram Fidger](hargram_fidger)** entered immediately after. 'I'm here to work with you.' **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**: 'Please don't come closer, I'm recovering.' 'We will meet again. My name is **[Hargram Fidger](hargram_fidger)**, I'm with the local **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** chapel.' He noted the guards around **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**. 'I think you're important with these guards.' 'We will have a better meeting another time.' He left. I have known **[Hargram Fidger](hargram_fidger)** since day twenty. His questions have always been too specific. He identified **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** as 'important' before any real conversation. **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** handled the interaction cleanly — cited recovery, deferred politely, dismissed without antagonising. Social competency under pressure: genuinely high.

subsections.title: Thornbury Reports — Aemenor Evenflight & The Portal Events (30 Harvestide, 1040)
subsections.description:
Before bed I told the group what I knew. Something is happening in the planar realms. I asked if they had met Aemenor Evenflight — the **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** called for reinforcements and he should be here. They said they'd met one of the **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)**'s captains. The timeline is confused. There are so many factions in this house now.

> **[The Planar Shards — What I Understand Now]** The shattered ritual on Highsun 21 — the party attempted a synchronisation rite with **[The Oracle](the_oracle)** to align the physical world, mirror-space, and the 'Deep Layers.' It catastrophically failed, tearing local reality into three planar shards. The FEYWARD Manor — a Feywild reflection where **[Lady Aurelian Corvinarus](lady_aurelian_corvinarus)** holds court, satyrs drink endlessly, and time moves strangely. The SHADEWARD Manor — a Shadowfell reflection where **[Orangus Cornelius](orangus_cornelius)** hosts vampire dinners and the Onyx Hand operates. And the MATERIAL Manor — where we are, where the **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** has established control and renamed the Vigilance to the Legionlance. The party was scattered across all three. **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** and Bowser went to the Shadowfell. **[Waluigi](waluigi)** and Toad Lee to the Feywild. Markop and Remi into the Deep Mirror. Toadburt was captured by the **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** in the physical antechamber — they fitted him with an Entropy Ring and sent him into the Feywild as a coerced agent with orders to capture **[The Oracle](the_oracle)** within three days.

> **[Sergeant Varn Coldbrook — **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** Fey Operations]** The **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** sent their own team through. Sergeant Varn Coldbrook — nineteen-year veteran who never expected to find himself in an impossible forest where the sun doesn't move. A practical man who believes in cold iron, hot meals, and following orders. His mission: locate and secure **[The Oracle](the_oracle)**. His squad entered the Feyward shard on Highsun 24 through a mirror-door a **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** wizard stabilised briefly. The door collapsed behind them. They've been trapped since. He started with eight soldiers. Private Henwick disappeared — found his boots arranged neatly beside a stream, facing upstream, no tracks. Corporal Dain started laughing during watch and hasn't stopped smiling — his eyes went the wrong colour. Private Marsh was replaced by something wearing his face. Coldbrook is down to five functional soldiers, none sleeping well, all jumping at sounds. He doesn't know we're in the same dimensional shard. He's been tracking unknown movement through the manor — building a picture of capabilities and intentions. He's also noticed the month-end deadline everyone keeps mentioning.

subsections.title: A New Day — Baths, Robes, and Byscilla Danos (29 Harvestide, 1040)
subsections.description:
29 Harvestide, 1040. Soldas. Golden Summer. Overcast, 28°C. I shook hands with **[Bones](bones)** — a real handshake, firm, acknowledged — as he cleared out the bathtub. I told **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** I would bring water from the well outside. I ran out, fetched two buckets, bubble bath, and rubber duckies. Morale is operational effectiveness by another name. I have been in this house for two weeks. I thought it would be welcome.

**[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** showered first. Clean dark blue mage's robe, brown belt, brown shoes, staff, third eye visible, hood down. He looked considerably more composed than someone who was unconscious and bleeding twelve hours ago has any right to look. **[Bones](bones)** said 'you look handsome.' **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**: 'what — it can't be that — umm — impressive right?' He was flustered. The most unguarded I've seen him.

**[Bones](bones)** went for a mirror, ran into someone. **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** — part of the **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** family. She wanted to know where the water-powered fans had gone. Her soldiers outside had heatstroke. **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** said 'it's just a bit of water, just a quick minute.' She was not persuaded. Then she saw ME.

> **[Cover Compromised — **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)**]** She said 'wait a minute — YOU!' and took me by the ear, dragging me out by my helmet. My cover with the **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** family is burned. My captain recognised me. She dragged me out of a room by my own helmet. **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** called after me: 'Thank you for helping us.' He had previously told the others he thought I might betray them. He thanked me in public while I was being dragged away. He is simultaneously suspicious and grateful and holds both states without needing to resolve them.

**[Bones](bones)** emerged from his shower unrecognisable — the mushroom had been obscuring him. He was genuinely happy. No one recognised him. **[Luigi](luigi)** came out last, mentioned he'd expelled ectoplasm in the bath, and no one reacted.
subsections.waluigi_note: Fetching bubble bath and rubber duckies for people you are spying on? WAH! Thornbury, you are too soft. Real spies use poison, not bubble bath!

subsections.title: ⚠ BREACH — They Found My Notes. They Read Everything. (29 Harvestide, 1040)
subsections.description:
> **[⚠ CONTAINMENT FAILURE]** After **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** removed me, **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** noticed something on the ground. I believe it fell from my kit during the dragging. He picked it up. He read the field notes. He described them as 'detailed notes on everything they did to the tee.' That is accurate. They were.

**[Bones](bones)**: 'He was a spy, wasn't he?' Silence. Cricket noises. **[Luigi](luigi)** walked out of the bath: 'huh?' 'He was spying on us.' 'How was the bath?' 'Bath was good, expelled ectoplasm too.' 'Well those notes are interesting I guess.' They all pulled up chairs and reviewed the contents of the notebook.

> **[Self-Assessment — Final Entry as Active Observer]** My cover is burned. Two weeks of careful observation, and they found the notes on the day I was dragged out by my own helmet. What they have read: everything. Every profile, every assessment, the ring I pocketed, the PL1 mortality note about **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** specifically. They have read that I know the clearing event might kill him and chose not to tell him.

If I am writing my own profile — and I am, because consistency requires it — I would note: subject was thorough and accurate. Subject concealed potentially fatal intelligence from a party member for operational reasons. Subject pocketed items without full disclosure. Subject fetched bubble bath and rubber duckies. Subject was dragged out by his helmet.

I do not assign morality scores. I assess effectiveness and reliability only. Being read was not effective. I need to do better.

What I am less certain about: whether 'better' means tighter operational security or something else. **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** thanked me. He knew I might betray him and he thanked me anyway. I am not used to that. I don't have a category for it.
subsections.waluigi_note: WAAAH! Leaving your secret diary on the bathroom floor is the most amateur mistake in the history of espionage. They read everything! Magnificent fail!

sections.name: Part II: Subject Clinical Profiles
sections.subtitle: Comprehensive Psychological & Tactical Diagnostics
sections.overview: Compiled by Thornbury from direct tactical observation. No moral judgments are made—only diagnostic assessments of combat effectiveness, reliability, and Guild cooperation levers.

subsections.title: ARCHIE MISER — Arcane caster / party lead
subsections.description:
**[Clinical Assessment — **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** — Full Assessment]**

Prior **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** contact confirmed (compass, name recognition). Elevated PL1 resonance risk.

STRENGTHS: Environmental observation when calm — found hidden doors without guidance. De-escalation under social pressure — the **[Hargram Fidger](hargram_fidger)** interaction was genuinely impressive. Resilience after trauma — requested watch shifts while bleeding. Extends trust early and does not obviously regret it.

WEAKNESSES: Magical offensive accuracy collapses under fear — zero for three on the ghost. Bravado precedes capability. Agreed to pay 2,062 gold for a rope. Will not pay.

INTERPERSONAL: Generous before being asked. Suspicious but patient — saw me pocket the ring and said nothing. Read notes describing his potential death and thanked me anyway. Either exceptional discipline or an unusual kind of grace.

**[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** COOPERATION: MODERATE TO HIGH. Follows the compass. Has prior connections. Fear of the **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** name is workable.

IF MISSION GOES WRONG: Will retreat, regroup, attempt to negotiate. Manageable through information — but he has now demonstrated he finds and reads field notes.

subsections.title: LUIGI — Support / Poltergust handler
subsections.description:
**[Clinical Assessment — **[Luigi](luigi)** — Full Assessment]**

Affiliation unclear. Bioluminescent flash capability.

STRENGTHS: Ghost absorption — the Poltergust is the most reliable anti-ghost capability in this party. Composure under all conditions. The flash clears rooms of multiple parties simultaneously. Correctly identified the practical solution (go around) while others climbed and fell.

WEAKNESSES: I haven't found any. This IS the concern.

INTERPERSONAL: Minimal verbal output. Expelled ectoplasm in the bath and mentioned it conversationally. Responded to discovering I was a spy with 'interesting I guess.'

**[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** COOPERATION: UNCERTAIN. No lever identified. No financial appetite, no institutional loyalty. He may simply continue operating regardless.

IF MISSION GOES WRONG: Do not underestimate the flash. Do not underestimate the Poltergust. Quietness is not passivity.

subsections.title: BONES — Melee combatant / Pond Patrol
subsections.description:
**[Clinical Assessment — **[Bones](bones)** — Full Assessment]**

Modified rapier. Refuses healing (unexplained, three times now).

STRENGTHS: Suplex, tackle, knockout — all confirmed. Environmental stealth when motivated. Makes tactically correct decisions without being asked. Warming to **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)** genuinely.

WEAKNESSES: Default answer to obstacles is force. Was stopped by a checkpoint during a chase. Refuses healing.

INTERPERSONAL: Distrusts Lucky T openly. Called me nice and I have filed this incorrectly twice.

**[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** COOPERATION: LOW. Loyalty is personal and individual. Do not engage directly without numerical advantage and a plan for the suplex.

subsections.title: SPEAKER L — Pond Patrol leadership
subsections.description:
**[Clinical Assessment — **[Speaker L](speaker_l)** — Full Assessment]**

Concealed hand crossbow. Results-driven, rule-agnostic post-Aegis Command.

STRENGTHS: Weekly cipher rotation, thorough dossiers. Concealed crossbow I did not detect. Political leverage from knowing how institutions fail. He sings operational briefings — genuinely effective for morale.

WEAKNESSES: Low night vision — **[Bones](bones)** had to steady him. Cover burned with at least one guard. Emotionally compromised around Aegis Command.

**[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** COOPERATION: VERY LOW. Will choose toad survival over **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** interests without hesitation. I would do the same in his position.

IF MISSION GOES WRONG: Will extract information and prioritise toad survival. Will not sacrifice himself for the party. Fully independent actor.

subsections.title: BYSCILLA DANOS — Mages Guild Captain
subsections.description:
**[Clinical Assessment — **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** — Assessment]**

My captain. **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** family — old money, **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)**-connected for generations. She is the working kind, not the inherited kind. Earned her captaincy through field operations, not patronage. Her squad trusts her in a way most **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** squads don't trust their captains.

She arrived with me on day one. She ran the survey. She told me not to get attached. She dragged me out by my helmet when she recognised me helping the party use **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** water resources for personal bathing. She was correct to do so. **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** resources are **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** resources.

She has been running the **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)**'s operational build-up at the manor quietly, in parallel with the party's activities. While the party explored, she mapped. While they fought ghosts, she catalogued. While they bathed, she reported. She is the person who will decide what happens to the PL1 fracture if the party fails. She has not shared her contingency plans with me. She does not share contingency plans with observers.

I trust her. I also know that trust is not something she factors into operational decisions. She factors effectiveness. And she is very, very effective.

sections.name: Part III: Manor Layout & Lore Compendium
sections.subtitle: Raventree Structural Blueprints & Cornelius Genealogy
sections.overview: A comprehensive structural directory detailing the Ground Floor, Second Floor, Attic, and Exterior Grounds of **[Raventree Manor](raventree_manor)**, combined with compiled dossiers on the **[Cornelius Family](the_oracle)** and the three planar shards.

subsections.title: MANOR LAYOUT — GROUND FLOOR
subsections.description:
**[Lore Source: Ground Floor Summary]**

R02 FOYER — Ruined marble, collapsed chandelier, grand staircases, root-blocked library doors. The guest book with Perrius Annmatar's entry 20 years ago. R03 HALLWAYS — West collapsed, east locked solid. Hidden passage to foyer. R04 LIBRARY — Immense, ransacked. Secret servant stair behind 'Useful Passages' book. Display case with three protected spell scrolls. Silver dagger (DC monogram). R05 OFFICE — Collapsed ceiling forms ramp to second floor. EC initials on bedframe. R06 STORAGE — Acid-trapped barrel. R07 WORKSHOP — Ylana's furniture stored after her death. The ring I pocketed. R08 GALLERY — The mirror. The formulae. **[The Oracle](the_oracle)**'s gateway. The Mole destroyed part of the inscription. R09 LOUNGE — Defaced portraits, ransacked drinks cabinet. Secret door to gallery. R10 VERANDA — Boot prints, shattered glass thrown 25+ feet. R11 KITCHEN — Five rust monsters. **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** says useful, I say absurd.

subsections.title: MANOR LAYOUT — SECOND FLOOR
subsections.description:
**[Lore Source: Second Floor Summary]**

R16 HALLWAY LANDING — Grand staircase landing, east/west split. R18 WESTERN LANDING — Reading nook, collapsed stairs to attic. Secret closet with peephole into Master Bathroom. R19 GUEST ROOMS — Five colour-coded rooms, Watcher's Hall between Blue and Red (illusory wall, one-way mirrors, silence enchantment). Guest lavatory. Secret collapsed stair to first floor. R20 LORD'S CHAMBERS — Ruined audience chamber, collapsed ceiling, grim host of spectral servants at night. Ochre Jelly in the lavatory. Spiral stair doors sealed. Servant's stairs end at hidden latch. R21 MASTER BEDROOM — Preserved by faltering spell. Immaculate desk. The Hidden Circle — broken teleportation circle under the rug. Key in desk drawer for library display case.

subsections.title: MANOR LAYOUT — ATTIC
subsections.description:
**[Lore Source: Attic Summary]**

S01 SOLARIUM — Rusting iron-and-glass ceiling, thousands of glass shards, mirrors arranged in a ring. Where the mirror entity was confronted. R24 BUTLER'S QUARTERS — Staff lounge, abandoned card game, secret passage via fake book. R25 BURN ROOM — Words carved into every surface by merged consciousness: 'trapped,' 'not me,' 'many,' 'alone.' R26 SENESCHAL'S ROOM — Shadow-burn silhouettes on furniture. A screaming face. Faceless servant portrait. Dust recently disturbed on mirrors. R23 SERVANT HALLWAYS — Trapped bathroom (thunder detonation). Most floors collapsed.

subsections.title: MANOR LAYOUT — EXTERIOR / GROUNDS
subsections.description:
**[Lore Source: Grounds Summary]**

COURTYARD — Wide, stone landing, great oaken doors with Corvinarus oak crest. Empty windows flank the entrance. NORTHERN PATH — Fountain with headless defaced statue. Mass grave in the flowerbeds — dozens of bodies, consecrated by a cleric who died afterward. GROUNDSKEEPER'S COTTAGE — Impassable hedge wall. Ten Wights shelter inside. DO NOT APPROACH. GREENHOUSE — Rusting, eastern grounds. **[Byscilla Danos](byscilla_danos)** noted but did not enter. THE GREAT TREE — Dead, webbed canopy, wrapped creatures hanging from branches. Giant spiders. Golden Knight statuette at base (mirror puzzle piece). MEMORIAL FOUNTAIN — In the hedge maze. Consecrated safe haven. Memorial to Ylana Annmatar. Magical water font. Small wooden bunny toy with 'Y.A.' and 'E.C.' initials.

subsections.title: THE THREE MANORS — PLANAR SHARDS
subsections.description:
**[Lore Source: Feyward / Shadeward / Material]**

MATERIAL MANOR: Where we are. **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** has established control. The Vigilance renamed the Legionlance. **[Mages' Guild](mages_guild)** operates in support role. PL1 fracture centred here.

FEYWARD MANOR: Feywild reflection. **[Lady Aurelian Corvinarus](lady_aurelian_corvinarus)** holds court. Eternal parties, drunken satyrs, sprites in greenhouses, a giant Guardian Butterfly, **[Wario](wario)**'s catalogue of absurd merchandise. The broken magic circle under the master bedroom rug connects here — estimated 4 days to repair, aligning with month-end. Sergeant Coldbrook's **[Iron Legion](iron_legion)** squad is trapped here with five of original eight soldiers.

SHADEWARD MANOR: Shadowfell reflection. **[Orangus Cornelius](orangus_cornelius)** hosts vampire dinners. The Onyx Hand operates. Monochrome reality. Fire magic doesn't work — **[Archie Miser](archie_miser)**'s primary offensive capability was nullified. Green T was held as a 'guest.' The Onyx Knight Kyrn offered friendship to Remi after her allies fled. Vivian haunts the corridors.

subsections.title: THE CORNELIUS FAMILY — COMPILED
subsections.description:
**[Lore Source: Family Tree & Key Figures]**

DRAGONUS CORNELIUS: Patriarch, 3 generations back. The statuette in the gallery bears his name.

DARIUS CORNELIUS: Orantha's contemporary — possibly husband or brother. Master wizard. The master bedroom desk, the component cabinet, the research journal. Obsessive organiser after losing Ylana. The inscription 'To my beloved daughter, that she may follow in my footsteps' in EC's textbook.

YLANA CORNELIUS (née Annmatar?): Lady of the house. Died — circumstances in the journal. Her furniture was moved to the workshop. Memorial fountain in the hedge maze. The gold bracelet. The music box in the closet. Perrius Annmatar's connection — family name match.
