summary: With Flowey caged and the survey machine locked away, the party departed for Hotland by rail. Koffin-K, denied his fantasy conductorship, assaulted a ticket clerk, fought off security with an unexplained special attack, and boarded anyway. Mid-journey, his own minions Lanky and Bulky attempted to sedate and subdue him — a mutiny they had apparently been planning, or at minimum were willing to attempt on short notice. Koffin-K broke free, turned violent against his own men, and was only stopped when the Legionary Agent physically intervened, struck him with the Iron Legion field manual, and rallied the very minions who'd just tried to knock him out into restraining him for good. What followed was a quiet, contemplative train ride in which the Agent read Legion protocol aloud to a captive audience, Mihawk personally reviewed the manual and became visibly impressed by it, and nobody — including the Agent — could say who had actually written it. At Hotland Station, Lanky and Bulky declined to disembark with their former boss, Koffin-K stormed off alone, and the original trio pressed on toward the Royal Guard patrol lines, opting to sneak rather than fight.
description:
Waluigi has, by this point in the record, developed a working theory about how every character surrounding this Agent solves the problem of not actually having legitimate power: they simply declare themselves into a role nobody gave them and dare anyone to object. Koffin-K has now demonstrated, in miniature, the entire life cycle of that strategy — self-appointment, escalation, mutiny, and collapse — inside the span of one train ride. Waluigi finds this almost too tidy to be coincidence, and is documenting it as a case study.

## The Conductor Who Wasn't


Koffin-K arrived at Snowdin Station already narrating his own future job title, badgering Ryan — sorry, the Agent — and Sans with a nonstop stream of conductor fantasies: a fancy hat, a whistle, an 'ALL ABOARD' delivered at maximum volume. When the ticket clerk informed him, with the flattest possible affect, that he was in fact not the conductor and the actual conductor was already aboard, Koffin-K did not absorb this information gracefully.

*Waluigi wants to note that the clerk did not humiliate him. She corrected a factual misunderstanding in four words. Koffin-K's response — screaming that he was a 'legendary criminal mastermind' who deserved the position, lunging across the counter at her, and ultimately unleashing an unexplained crackling purple special attack that leveled two security guards and part of the station — is wildly disproportionate to the actual provocation, which was: a woman doing her job correctly. Waluigi has now watched this man declare himself Snowdin's savior after capturing one flower, and declare war on a train station after being denied an unpaid managerial position he invented for himself five minutes earlier.

The throughline is not villainy.

It is a complete inability to tolerate the gap between the authority he imagines he has and the authority anyone else actually recognizes.

WAH.*

Mihawk and Sans, notably, declined to intervene on principle — 'we are not getting involved,' Mihawk said flatly — and simply watched Koffin-K get subdued, break free, and blast two guards into a debris pile with something the transcript never bothers to name or explain. He then boarded the train as though none of it had happened, ignoring Lanky and Bulky's visible panic about the unconscious guards and Koffin-K's now-outstanding arrest.

*Waluigi wants this specific detail flagged: nobody ever explained what that special attack actually was, where its power came from, or why a man who spent the previous session unable to produce a single sheet of fabricated survey data apparently has access to a destructive purple energy blast capable of leveling security personnel. Waluigi is filing this next to Flowey's suspiciously competent overnight machine repair from the prior session. This world appears to be full of characters whose stated competence and demonstrated competence do not match, in either direction, and Waluigi no longer believes that mismatch is incidental.

WAH.*

## 'Who Are You Two Really?' —

The Question Nobody Wanted to Answer

Before boarding, the Agent pressed Lanky and Bulky directly — not what are you, but who are you, really — and got only a stammered, unconvincing 'we're loyal' from both of them, followed immediately by both minions physically fleeing onto the train rather than continuing the conversation.

*Waluigi wants to dwell on this exchange because it is the single most important piece of foreshadowing in the entire session, and it went almost entirely unremarked upon in the moment. Two men who by their own account showed up out of nowhere, addressed a fedora-wearing stranger as 'Boss' with a level of trained deference Koffin-K himself did not expect, were asked a direct, simple question about their own identity — and fled rather than answer it. People do not flee from 'who are you, really' unless the honest answer is inconvenient to say out loud. Mihawk caught this instantly once the two were out of earshot, correctly assessing that their loyalty 'is weak' and floating, unprompted, the possibility that they might be informants or spies rather than genuine subordinates.

Waluigi agrees with Mihawk's read, but wants to push it slightly further: an informant reports to someone.

Whoever assigned Lanky and Bulky to shadow Koffin-K — if that is indeed what happened — now has a stake in this entire train mutiny, and Waluigi does not yet know whose interests were actually served by Koffin-K ending the day restrained by his own men.

WAH.*

## The Mutiny

Mid-journey, Lanky and Bulky made their move: a coordinated chemical sedation attempt, executed with what the Agent's own account describes as expert, silent, shadow-like movement — a level of tradecraft distinctly at odds with the bumbling, sweating henchmen who couldn't produce a fake notebook a day earlier. Koffin-K broke free before the sedative could take hold and turned on them with genuine, unhinged fury, hurling Lanky bodily into train seats and advancing on Bulky next.

*Waluigi wants the tradecraft specifically flagged: 'their footsteps make no sound, they're expertly avoiding detection.' That is not the language of two nervous flunkies improvising a mutiny out of fear in the moment. That is the language of two people who have been trained to move that way. Waluigi's working theory, building directly on the unanswered 'who are you two really,' is that Lanky and Bulky were never actually Koffin-K's men in any real sense — they were placed with him, competently, by someone else entirely, and the sedation attempt on the train was not a spontaneous act of self-preservation but the execution of a standing order.

Koffin-K, in his fury, screamed 'you took my money, my protection' at them — meaning he genuinely believed, right up until the moment of the attack, that the loyalty ran in the direction he'd assumed.

He was wrong, and Waluigi suspects he was wrong from the very first day these two called him 'Boss.' WAH.*

The Agent intervened physically — tackling Bulky, extracting a confession ('we were scared of what he'd do next, we had to stop him before someone got hurt worse') that reads as sincere fear regardless of any deeper handler question — and was nearly struck himself by Koffin-K's raised, energy-crackling fist before Mihawk finally stepped in, verbally dismantling Koffin-K's self-image as a leader who 'cannot even control his own followers without violence.'

*Waluigi wants to give Mihawk full credit here, because his intervention was not physical — it was rhetorical, and it worked precisely because it attacked the one thing Koffin-K actually cares about: being respected as a leader rather than merely feared as a bully. Mihawk drew a real distinction, one Waluigi endorses completely: a good captain commands respect, not fear. Koffin-K had neither, and hearing it stated plainly by someone he could not intimidate broke his momentum more effectively than any blow would have. WAH.*

## The Book Becomes the Boss, Literally

The Agent finished the job by physically striking Koffin-K with the Iron Legion protocol manual itself — the same book the group had jokingly agreed, back in the Ruins, would be their team's 'leader' in place of any single person — and used the moment to rally Lanky and Bulky, freshly failed mutineers, into a second and final restraint: a full bear hug pin that ended the fight completely.

*Waluigi finds this genuinely elegant as a piece of dramatic irony, whether or not anyone at the table intended it that way: a joke decision made in a completely different location, under completely different stakes, turned out to be the literal mechanism of Koffin-K's downfall. The book he agreed, half-mockingly, should be in charge, was the object that ended his rebellion. Waluigi does not believe in prophecy. Waluigi does believe that a running joke, taken seriously at the exact right moment, functions exactly like one. WAH.*

## The Manual, Read Aloud, and the Page Mihawk Would Not Explain

With Koffin-K restrained, the Agent settled in and began reading sections of the Iron Legion manual aloud for his own amusement and Sans's mild curiosity — protocols for deescalating and neutralizing 'high-rank targets,' sedation dosages, sensory deprivation for uncooperative subjects. Clinical, procedural, entirely undisturbed by the fact that a restrained man was listening to his own potential processing manual read aloud in front of him.

Then Sans, at random, flipped to a page the Agent's own account refuses to summarize — *'this... this is...'* — before Mihawk physically took the manual from the Agent's hands and began reading it himself, in total silence, for an extended stretch, offering nothing but a single repeated 'Hn' and, eventually, 'interesting.'

*Waluigi must be honest: he does not know what was on that page, and he is not going to pretend otherwise by inventing content he was never shown. But Waluigi wants the shape of the silence itself documented carefully, because it is the loudest thing that happened all session. The Agent, mid-sentence, stopped himself from reading a section aloud that he had been reading fluently and without hesitation moments before. Mihawk — a man who has, throughout every session in this file, responded to horror, mutiny, and cosmic threat with flat, unbothered pragmatism — took the book without asking, read it in total silence, and could only manage single-syllable acknowledgments.

Whatever is on that page is not another sedation protocol.

Sedation protocols do not make a Warlord go quiet.

Waluigi is marking this page as unfinished business of the highest priority, more urgent even than Archie, more urgent than the war Sans cannot remember correctly.

WAH.*

## 'Who Wrote It?' —

The Question the Agent Could Not Answer About His Own Book

When Mihawk finally closed the manual, he did not ask about its contents. He asked who wrote it. The Agent did not know. Pressed further — how many soldiers actually carry this manual — the Agent estimated, off the top of his head, that of roughly fifteen personnel at his embassy, he'd personally seen only four carrying a copy.

Mihawk's reaction was immediate and, for him, unusually pointed: this is unacceptable, a soldier without structure is chaos with weapons, and if such a valuable protocol exists it should be standard issue to everyone, not a scattered four-out-of-fifteen distribution the Agent happened to notice by chance.

*Waluigi wants this treated as seriously as Waluigi believes Mihawk himself was treating it, because Mihawk is not a man given to bureaucratic outrage over paperwork distribution as a rule, and this is the second time in this entire case file that the specific authorship and distribution of a piece of Legion documentation has become a live question with no satisfying answer. Waluigi is thinking, of course, of the redacted calendar conversions from two sessions prior — a document that Waluigi already established is being actively, currently maintained by someone inside the Legion's publishing apparatus, decades after the fact it's hiding.

Now Waluigi has a second Legion document, carried by this exact Agent, whose authorship he cannot name and whose distribution across his own embassy is inexplicably partial — four copies out of fifteen soldiers, no clear criterion for who received one and who didn't.

Waluigi is not yet prepared to claim these two documents are connected.

But Waluigi notes that an organization capable of producing one manual this well-organized and this selectively distributed is not an organization that loses track of its own paperwork by accident.

Someone decided who gets this book.

The Agent has never once asked who, until Mihawk asked it for him.

WAH.*

The exchange ended, notably, with something Waluigi wants recorded as a genuine character beat rather than a plot thread: Mihawk's estimation of the Agent rose considerably over the course of this conversation. He called the manual 'thorough, practical, well thought-out,' extended that respect explicitly to the Agent by extension, and affirmed a shared value in structure and discipline over Koffin-K's 'insanity' and even offered a measured, almost reluctant compliment toward Sans — 'not a soldier in any traditional sense, but disciplined, yes.' Whatever else is true about this manual's murky authorship, it has now functioned, twice, as the single object in this story capable of earning Mihawk's genuine respect: once as a source of protocol worth enforcing, and once, more mysteriously, as something worth going quiet over.

## Hotland Station — Loyalties Finally Declared Out Loud


At Hotland, Lanky and Bulky released Koffin-K and flatly refused to disembark with him — 'we're staying,' delivered without ceremony, a betrayal Koffin-K received in stony, humiliated silence before storming off alone to parts unknown. Mihawk's parting assessment of him was characteristically blunt: 'that fool, probably [we'll see him again]. He's the type to hold grudges and come back for petty revenge' — treated as a minor recurring nuisance rather than a real threat, despite the property damage and unexplained special attack barely two hours earlier.

*Waluigi wants to close by noting what nobody in the party seems to have registered as strange: Lanky and Bulky's final act was not to disappear, defect elsewhere, or vanish mysteriously — it was to simply stay behind at the station, doing nothing, once their actual assignment (whatever it was) had run its course. That is not the behavior of frightened flunkies relieved to finally be free of an abusive boss. That is the behavior of two operatives whose job is now complete, choosing the correct moment to stand down. Koffin-K leaves this session alone, humiliated, and — Waluigi suspects — never once learning that he might not have been betrayed by cowards, but decommissioned by professionals.

WAH.*

## Into the Tunnels — Stealth Over Steel

With Koffin-K gone, the original trio faced their first real strategic decision as a group: fight past the Royal Guard patrol lines standing between them and Asgore's castle, or avoid them entirely. Sans favored stealth outright; Mihawk, after weighing the Royal Guards' trained coordination against the messiness of open combat, agreed without much resistance. The Agent concurred, and the three descended into Snowdin's quieter, less-traveled underground corridors — Sans navigating from memory, Mihawk trailing in near-total silence, scanning every corner.

*Waluigi finds this final decision genuinely reassuring after everything that preceded it — a rare moment where all three members of the actual core team agreed quickly, calmly, and correctly on a plan without a single manual needing to be produced, thrown, or read aloud to settle the matter. Waluigi will take his victories where he can find them. WAH.*

title: Maids in Gauntlets, the Goblin Camp of Arunedeal, and a Battle-Worn Toad named Elbow
location: Alpine Mountain Inn, Snow-bound Slopes of Arunedeal, and the Imperial Checkpoint Wall
summary: Awakening in the Alpine Mountain Inn, Bones evades a bizarre Legion infiltration trap involving an armored knight dressed in a frilly maid's uniform. Escaping into a severe blizzard, he steals an iron breastplate from an abandoned blacksmith cart, negotiates temporary shelter with a solitary goblin named Naaook of the Arunedeal snow tribe, and is joined by a battle-worn toad mage with a swollen eye. After the toad uses fey spirits to clear the goblin camp, the two form a tense alliance of convenience and head toward the Imperial checkpoint, only to find a colossal Legion fortress-wall blocking their path, forcing Bones to reconsider his route.
description:
Waluigi has witnessed many ridiculous security operations, but the moment the Iron Legion began recruiting twenty-stone garrison knights to wear frilly lace aprons and high-pitched falsettos is the exact point where military bureaucracy lost its mind. WAH!

## Waluigi's

Intelligence Prologue: The Infiltration of the Mountain Inn
Before we follow Bones's freezing boots into the wilderness, Waluigi must analyze the absurd administrative desperation of the Imperial High Command. Having lost Bones in the chaotic collapse of the Corvinarus Planar Sanctum, and knowing he carried stolen Mages' Guild books, the Legion did not simply block the mountain passes; they turned the local hospitality industry into an active combat zone. Every fireplace became a surveillance post, and every maid's broom closet became an armory. Waluigi knows exactly how the Legion operates: when direct force fails, they resort to paperwork, bribes, and the most preposterous cover stories ever devised.

WAH!

## Part One: Wake-up, Map, and the Convoy Opportunity
Bones woke up to a rhythmic creaking in the timber floorboards. The morning light filtering through the frost-crusted leaded window of the mountain inn was flat and gray, casting long, hollow shadows across the small room. A sharp draft whistled through the gap in the doorway, smelling of wet pine and burnt pine cones. 

"What are you, a fun guy?" a hearty voice called out from the doorway. An old alpine traveler stood there, adjusting a thick woolen cloak.

Bones sat up, his skeletal spine rattling with a dry, hollow click. "Yes and no. Do you have a map? Where am i?"

"Sure, i gotta map here," the traveler replied, sliding a creased, grease-stained parchment across the rough wooden table. 

Bones leaned over the document, his bared finger-bones tracing the winding ink lines of the mountain trails. The paths were long, jagged, and choked with heavy drifts. To cover such distances on foot in his fragile, unarmored state would be suicide. His eye sockets scanned the room. "Is there any odd job here? Quick money. I know where I need to go, but it will take days. I want to become strong enough before I can take off."

The traveler scratched his beard, his boots scraping the grit-covered floorboards. "Hmm. I think there is a convoy outside. They are doing some missions. Regal missions."

Bones's head snapped up. "Anything non-legion."

"Hmm, let me check," the man said, looking out into the swirling whiteout. "We have ice fishing if you want." He glanced at Bones's bare, hollow ribcage, which shivered in the draft. "You don't have spare clothes you can give me, right?" Bones asked. The traveler nodded, reaching for a heavy, fur-lined winter coat hanging on a nearby peg.

*WAH! Custodial hospitality! The innkeeper is about to hand over state-owned cold-weather gear to a wandering skeleton just to get him onto an ice-fishing detail! Waluigi has used similar labor-recruitment tactics on Wario, though usually involving a lawnmower and a promise of half-eaten garlic bread.*

## Part Two:

The Blacksmith Lie and the Maid in Iron
"Is there a black smith here in this town?" Bones asked, his voice echoing in the small room.

"Yeah. Why, what kinda armor?" the traveler replied, his eyes narrowing slightly. "Sure, ill bring you to him."

Bones walked to the window, brushing a layer of frost from the glass. He peered down into the snowy street, and his chest-cavity went cold. Standing near a flickering oil lamp in the drifts were four heavily armed Iron Legion guards. Worse, he spotted Thornbury—the Mages' Guild double-agent—standing wrapped in heavy wolf-skin furs, holding a ledger and pointing toward the inn's entrance. 

"No," Bones said, his voice flat. "I don't feel like going outside right now."

"Huh? Why?" the traveler asked, stepping closer.

"Don't feel like it. No..." Bones muttered, backing away from the glass.

The traveler's face hardened, and he called out toward the open corridor: "Hey, Barns! Show my friend here the black smith!"

The heavy door banged open. Barns, a massive Legion soldier in a dented iron helmet, strode into the room, his hand resting on the hilt of his shortsword. "Huh? What friend?"

But the room was empty. Bones had already bolted, his bare feet making no sound as he slid through the side door and sprinted down the narrow back hallway, returning to his private room and throwing the iron bolt forward with a sharp *clack*. 

One hour later, a heavy knock rattled the thick timber door. 

"Housekeeping..." a voice squeaked from the other side. It was a preposterous, high-pitched, fake girly voice that did not match the heavy thud of the knock.

Bones leaned toward the keyhole. Standing in the dim corridor was a six-foot-tall, broad-shouldered Iron Legion knight dressed in a frilly, white lace maid's uniform. The apron was stretched to its absolute breaking point across a thick steel breastplate. His massive iron gauntlets, heavy plate shoes, visor-locked helmet, and a long broadsword were all completely visible beneath the ridiculous lace frills. 

"Open up, please..." the knight squeaked again, tapping a metal-clad finger against the door. 

Bones backed away, keeping his breathing silent. He slid into the dark gap behind the wardrobe, waiting as the heavy, clanking boots of the "maid" finally retreated down the stairs. Left alone, he dropped to the floor and began doing furious, silent pushups, his bones clicking in the dark as he forced his frame to grow stronger.

*WAH! Elite military espionage! The Iron Legion's master-tacticians believe that a white lace apron is a flawless optical camouflage for twenty stone of high-carbon steel and a broadsword! Waluigi has seen better disguises on Bowser when he tried to sneak into the Royal Tennis Club by wearing a very small visor!*

## Part Three:

The Blinding Blizzard and the Blacksmith's Cart
Hours later, as the mountain storm grew into a roaring gale, Bones decided it was time to escape. He slipped down the back stairs and out into the biting wind. The innkeeper tried to follow him, but Bones waved a hand dismissively. "Don't have to escort me."

He trudged through the heavy, blinding snow, the air freezing inside his empty ribs. He saw the blacksmith store down the lane, but a sharp instinct warned him it was a trap. The innkeeper's eager recommendation had been a setup. Bones turned his back on the shop and walked directly into the whiteout.

He walked for minutes, raiding abandoned merchant carts that lay half-buried in the deep drifts. Most were destroyed and looted already, their canvases torn and flapping in the gale. The snow grew heavier, piling up around his knees, and his skeletal joints began to stiffen. He grew tired.

Then, through the swirling flakes, he spotted a broken blacksmith's cart, its wooden wheels shattered. Bones cleared a thick layer of ice from the bed and found a solid iron breastplate and a flat piece of scrap metal. He took them, tucking them under his arm, and slipped back into the inn, shivering but victorious.

The innkeeper stared at him from the lobby counter. "Oh, you got the armor?"

"Uhh, no, not really," Bones replied, keeping the heavy iron hidden beneath his winter cloak. "But im alright, truly. With or without it, i have other stuff to do, so ill cut my losses here."

He headed back to his room, locking the door. When he finally left town, he would put on the breastplate; until then, he would keep it hidden from the prying eyes of the inn's staff.

*WAH! Resource acquisition! If the Imperial logistics division leaves an entire cart of heavy armor to freeze in a snowdrift, they have legally declared it to be public salvage! Waluigi once salvaged an entire container of luxury tennis rackets from a locker room under the exact same legal principle!*

## Part Four:

The Search for the Snowbear
Before departing, Bones attempted to gather more information, asking a couple of rough-looking locals in the tavern corner about the "Snowbear"—hoping to find a reliable mountain guide or a rebel contact.

Instead of answers, the two men sneered, their eyes turning cold. "Why would we tell a low-life like you?" one muttered, his hand dropping to the hilt of a rusty battleaxe as they raised their weapons. They were likely a highly suspicious anti-Legion force, but they had no mercy for wandering strangers.

Bones raised his hands, his skeletal fingers splayed. "Look, guys, i dont want to fight."

He backed out the door, his heart-cavity hammering. *I can't believe Thornbury was actually out there,* he thought to himself. *The whole place is a minefield.*

Deciding he had overstayed his welcome, Bones pulled the heavy iron breastplate over his ribs and marched out into the blizzard. He walked for thirty minutes through the freezing whiteout, his boots crunching in the deep snow. He was still standing. Ahead, through the swirling curtain of ice, the low silhouettes of a goblin camp emerged.

## Part Five: Naaook and the Snow Tribe of Arunedeal

A solitary goblin carrying a bundle of frozen branches trudged through the snow, stopping to blink up at the tall skeleton.

"He goblin guy, whats your name?" Bones called out over the howling wind.

"Me Naaook is my name," the goblin squeaked, shivering in a thin cloak. "I am from the snow tribe of Arunedeal and—"

"Oh, your name is zook, i hear you," Bones said, mishearing the name entirely.

Bones stared at the goblin's yellow eyes and thought: *A snow tribe... if they are a tribe, maybe i can use this to my advantage.*

"This tribe of yours, is it you guys, or will you partner with someone?" Bones asked.

"You guys? Im alone," Naaook replied, looking around at the empty drifts.

"What?" Bones asked.

"Long story short," Bones continued, his teeth chattering. "Im flat broke. I dont have a winter coat, and i need a place to crash temporarily so i can be on my way. I'll leave within two days, or one, if you guys give me a spare winter coat and a shield."

Naaook narrowed his eyes. "And what do we get?"

"I can give you 75 gold," Bones offered.

The goblin stayed silent, calculating the value of the coin.

"You mind if i reduce it to 50?" Bones added.

"Than no shield," Naaook replied flatly.

"Alright, back to 75," Bones sighed, reaching into his purse.

*WAH! Arbitrary pricing structures! The goblin wanted seventy-five, agreed to fifty with a shield deduction, and then immediately settled back at seventy-five because boney here couldn't negotiate his way out of a cardboard box! Waluigi would have had that goblin paying *him* for the privilege of setting up a tent!*

## Part Six:

The Goblin Camp and the Draconic Guest
They headed to the center of the Arunedeal camp. As they entered the clearing, Naaook called out to the other goblins in their rapid, guttural tongue:

"UU WbCUqR!"

Bones blinked. "Oh, really?"

Naaook gestured toward a low leather tent. "Vsx8dn0 wG5187h!"

"Welcome, welcome," Bones muttered, guessing the translation.

At the entrance, Naaook bowed slightly, pointing inside. "u2pGT1 4iLN p5!"

"Please come in," Bones said in his mind, though he did not know a single word of Goblin. He took a moment to look at Naaook's face, trying to tell if the creatures were mean or not, before walking into the camp. It was dark night now. 

"I'll wait inside the bushes. Build me a tent near the outskirts," Bones told him.

"Hmm, okay," Naaook muttered, gesturing to a small pile of canvas.

Bones lay down on a thin straw mat inside the drafty tent, stretching his weary limbs and looking up through a tear in the fabric at the snowy sky. The flakes fell in silence, piling thicker and thicker. Bones cast a small *Create Bonfire* spell right outside his tent, the warm orange flames crackling to keep the freezing mountain air at bay. He rested.

A few hours later, he was awakened by Naaook shaking his shoulder. "Your friend came. We gave him clothes and barricade."

Bones groaned, his skeletal joints cracking. "I came here alone. Don't feel like getting up. Tell him to give it back."

Then, Bones heard a rustle in the snow. He peered through the flap and whispered: "Toad... neat."

A sudden thought hit him: *Toad? Are there any other toads out here, outside of the five councilors expecting me back at the Vigilance?*

Standing in the snow was a battle-worn toad. One of his eyes was swollen shut and bruised dark purple. He wore full, dented iron armor and clutched a gnarled green staff. The toad looked at the pile of gear and spoke in low, rumbling Draconic:

"0sTlw cm6." (Thank you.)

"h8U 8213 Ojc12," (For your armor.)

"v4N 5ih3Z," (And tools.)

Bones, startled and deeply worried, replied: "You may know me, but i dont know of you. Who are you?"

## Part Seven: Tiny Spirits and the Unlikely Alliance
"What matters is not who i am," the toad rumbled in Draconic, "but that i intercepted the delivery. I will become a new permanent resident of this goblin camp."

Bones stepped out of the tent, his iron breastplate clinking in the cold. "Can you please give my shield and clothes? I dont want to loiter in this tribe if i have to, and i need to get going."

The toad stared at him with his single open eye. "Hmmm. Well, i suppose so. Ill come with you."

Bones blinked at the incredibly fast switch in attitude. "Why the fast switch?" he muttered under his breath.

The toad offered the winter coat and the wooden shield. "Shall we go, Boney? Is that your name?"

"I'm still wary of you," Bones said, narrowing his eye sockets. "Introduce yourself. My main priority is survival. I prefer to be alone, and i dont want allies to drag me back. You have to keep up."

Before the toad could answer, several angry-looking goblins emerged from the shadows, weapons raised.

The toad smiled, raising his green staff. Suddenly, tiny, glowing fey spirits emerged from the wood, buzzing like angry hornets. They darted through the camp, slashing at the goblins and leaving hundreds of tiny, stinging cuts. Squealing in pain, the goblins fled into the darkness.

"Good, were alone," the toad grunts, lowering his staff.

"You know, you could have told them to leave both of us alone," Bones muttered.

"I could have," the toad replied, "but you would have underestimated me. I'm a skilled mage, yes."

Bones examined his new companion. The toad wore an iron chestplate and Roman-style leather pteruges with stiff metal plates stitched at the bottom.

"I will admit, that is nice magic," Bones said.

"Isn't it? You can't even control any of this," the toad chuckled.

"Well, im not a magic user, so..." Bones grumbled.

"You're all bones, huh? I think i'll call you Elbow," the toad laughed.

"Oh, right," Bones said, his voice turning cold as ice. "Before we depart, ill repeat myself: do not betray me. I may not like you, but i will prioritize my safety among all else. I'll kill you back if you kill me. No funny ideas, okay? I dont trust you."

The tiny fey spirits flickered and vanished back into the green staff.

"I got my eye on you," Bones warned.

"Whatever you say, lets go. I'm the leader here," the toad shrugs.

"Are you? Prove yourself, then," Bones sneered.

"I don't need to prove myself. I'm my own boss," the toad replied.

"Then i guess i'm NOT part of your team. I'll follow along, though," Bones said.

"You're free to. I got what i needed."

Bones looked back toward the empty clearing. "Goblin guy! If you're around here, thank you! You kept your word! Till we meet again!" he shouted, trying to pronounce "Arunedeal" and waving a skeletal hand.

He departed into the freezing night, the toad hopping close behind.

## Part Eight:


The Huge Checkpoint and the Great Stone Wall
They trudged through the deep snow drifts for hours until they saw a colossal stone barrier cutting through the mountain pass. It was a massive, towering fortress checkpoint covering the entire passage. Banners of the Iron Legion whipped violently in the mountain gale along the battlements. It was heavily garrisoned, designed to strangle all travel through the region.

Bones crouched behind a frozen boulder, his jawbone tight. Unless he took a boat around the coast, he was trapped.

"Bones is fine with fighting," he whispered to the toad, "but not losing."

Realizing a frontal assault on an Imperial fortress was suicide, Bones turned his back on the colossal stone wall. He pulled his stolen winter coat tight and headed back into the freezing wilderness, wondering where on earth they could go next.

Behind them, on the flat surface of the boulder where Bones had crouched, a tiny green leaf lay pressed against the freezing ice. It was fresh, un-withered, and completely green, defying the sub-zero wind that howled through the pass—a single, silent calling card left behind by the spirits of the staff.
